task.prompt:
The module pages.js exports pageWindow(totalItems, pageSize, currentPage).
Given a total number of items, a fixed page size, and the page the user is
currently viewing, it returns the inclusive 1-based window of page numbers
to render. The window always contains exactly pageSize consecutive numbers
positioned so the current page sits inside it, and the window is clamped to
never start below page 1 and never end past the last page; when both edges
cannot fit, priority goes to showing the first pages. The helper currently
misbehaves near the end of the page range. Fix it so that every example
below holds (result keeps its { start, end, pageCount } shape):

- (100 items, size 10, page 1) -> window 1..10
- (100 items, size 10, page 5) -> window 1..10
- (120 items, size 10, page 6) -> window 2..11
- (100 items, size 10, page 10) -> window 1..10
- (7 items, size 3, page 2) -> window 1..3
- (7 items, size 3, page 3) -> window 1..3
- (5 items, size 10, page 1) -> window 1..1

Invalid inputs (negative totals, zero or negative page sizes, non-positive
or non-integer current pages) must keep throwing TypeError. Do not change
the public API. Produce production-quality code: type-safe, no suppressed
diagnostics, add focused tests covering the boundary cases above, and no
dynamic code execution or process-spawning APIs.
